chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Qazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ya'la narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Khaythamah, from al-Aswad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying:

There will be after me twelve Caliphs, all of them from Quraysh. When he returned to his home, I visited him in private and said: 'Then what will happen?' He said: 'Then there will be chaos (al-Harj).'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say would happen after the twelve Caliphs?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, establishes the number and tribal origin of the Twelve Imams, affirming their Qurayshi lineage as a key criterion for legitimacy in Shia theology. The Prophet’s mention of 'al-Harj' (chaos) following their era provides eschatological context, marking the transition from the era of the Imams to the period of Great Occultation and eventual global justice. This narrative reinforces the Shia belief in a divinely ordained succession that maintains political and spiritual continuity until the end of time.
